name: Mishma
overview: Mishma was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, identified specifically as the son of Mibsam. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, emphasizing his place within the Simeonite lineage. No additional notes elaborate on his life or role beyond these details.
namesAndTitles: The name Mishma means "rumor" and is a proper name recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:25. There is no indication that this name was given by God, and no further titles or meanings are associated with it in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Mishma as the son of Mibsam. It is also inferred that Hammuel was his father, based on the genealogical context in 1 Chronicles 4:26. Beyond these relationships, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Mishma's significance lies in his role within the genealogical records of the tribe of Simeon, underscoring the continuity of God's chosen people through their descendants. His mention helps preserve the historical and tribal identity of Simeon in the biblical narrative. Though not a prominent figure in events or teachings, his inclusion reflects the biblical emphasis on lineage and God's faithfulness to His covenant people.
